reasons: spec.md's Acceptance says a unit test proves 'the same three outcomes' (undeclared fails, declared-via-Files-that-change ok, declared-via-Proof-item ok) for the eval-case drop, but plan.md's Proof list only names test_ratchets_drop_eval_case_folder_emptied_fails and test_ratchets_drop_eval_case_dot_rename_fails — both prove only the undeclared-fail outcome. No test anywhere in the Proof list proves that a plan-declared eval-case drop (via 'Files that change' listing the case folder, including the trailing-slash directory match Design calls out, or via a '- ratchet: evals' Proof line) is ok. This is the one declaration path most likely to carry its own bug (directory-level matching instead of single-file matching) and it ships with zero test coverage, contradicting spec.md Requirements' own rule 'every behavior above ships with a test that fails without it.'

spec.md Requirements defines a dropped test file as 'a D ... or an R whose source matches a glob and whose destination matches none.' Only the D case (test_ratchets_drop_test_file_undeclared_fails) and the rename-that-is-NOT-a-drop case (test_ratchets_rename_within_test_paths_is_not_a_drop) are in plan.md's Proof; spec.md's own Acceptance section never asks for, and plan.md's Proof never supplies, a test where an R's destination does NOT match any test_paths glob and is therefore a drop. A bug that silently exempts a renamed-away test file from the drop rule would pass every listed test.

The skip-marker scan's Requirements name two scan surfaces: files under test_paths, and the test-runner's own configuration files (pytest.ini, pyproject.toml's pytest section, setup.cfg, tox.ini, conftest.py, package.json's jest block, jest.config.*). plan.md's Proof (test_ratchets_skip_markers_listed_never_fail) only exercises the first surface, using this repository's own runbook test files as fixture; no test exercises the configuration-file scanning path at all, even though that path needs separate per-format parsing (a jest block inside package.json, a pytest section inside pyproject.toml) that the test-file path does not.
classification_reasons: Blast radius is large: plan.md's Files that change reaches core gate infrastructure used at every phase (c)/(d)/(e) gate for every project on the plugin (plugin/gate/checks.py, plugin/gate/diff.py, plugin/state/unpark.py, plugin/pr/description.py), plus the adversarial-reviewer agent, two templates/skills and OPERATING_MODEL — well beyond 'few files', even though no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is nominally touched.

The code this design prescribes (a rename-aware --name-status -M parser, a committed-tree tree_files helper, a new gate check, cross-check union logic in unpark.py, a plan-at-merge-base declaration reader) is wholly new; no existing test in the suite exercises any of it today, so 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold.

The spec is not yet tight: this same design round already needed a substantive correction (panel decision #2, the eval-case drop rule could not be implemented from diff records alone) and this review finds the Proof list still does not cover two behaviors spec.md itself states as requirements (the eval-case declared-ok paths, the R-is-a-drop case for test files) plus an untested scan surface (config files). That is the opposite of 'no open concern.'
attempted: Intent: compared intent.md's Proposed outcome bullet by bullet against spec.md's Requirements/Design and plan.md; the shape of the fix (parallel ratchets check, unpark.py union, plan-declared exemption, risk-list-shaped hit, skip-marker listing) matches intent.md throughout; no substitution found at that level.

Spec and plan: checked that the plan edits requested in the fix round (fix-response.md) actually landed — confirmed plan.md 'Files that change' line 35-38 and Order of work step 9 now bump .claude-plugin/marketplace.json together with plugin.json, and Proof now contains test_ratchets_plan_edited_after_merge_base_does_not_excuse_drop, test_ratchets_risk_list_tests_configured_does_not_satisfy_ratchet_hit, and the amended test_ratchets_skip_markers_listed_never_fail naming the runbook-file fixture explicitly — all three match the owner's PR #186 review comment and fix-response.md's description. Then went past the fix round to re-check spec.md's Acceptance against plan.md's Proof line by line for every stated behavior, which surfaced the three gaps above: the eval-case declared-ok outcomes, the test-file rename-is-a-drop case, and the skip-marker config-file scan surface, none of which plan.md's Proof section names a test for even though spec.md's own Requirements/Acceptance describe them as behaviors to ship.

Flagged concerns: both concerns in spec.md are marked [x] closed via the two panel decisions recorded in decisions-b.md/decisions-b.json (framework/-scope confirmed structurally; eval-case survivor-vs-drop gap closed by adding the tree_files helper and a new Proof test) — both closures are reflected consistently in spec.md's Design and plan.md's Risks/Proof, no contradiction found there.

Proof vs diff: read the diff-b.patch --stat header and confirmed this commit touches only spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml and evidence/* — no plugin/template/docs source file is edited yet, correct for a phase-(b) design-only commit; the actual code and its tests are deferred to phase (c) as the plan's Order of work describes.

Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is touched; the new check's files are all named in plan.md's 'Files that change' with no surprise scope expansion.

Policies: security-baseline rules 2/6 (no shell string, no shell=True) are respected by the diff.py helper design (argument-list git invocation via the existing _git helper); data-conventions and most ux-conventions are correctly marked not-applicable with stated reasons (no stored field/PII, no UI surface).

Tests: walked every Requirements bullet against spec.md's Acceptance and then against plan.md's Proof list to find any behavior with no named test; found the three gaps listed in reasons. Did not rely on, or cite, the runner's own prior claude-b.json/run-b.json/gate-b.json or the earlier adversarial-review-b.json (written for an earlier HEAD, 9d4301b) as evidence for or against this HEAD — those were read only for historical context on what the fix round changed, and this verdict is based on an independent re-read of spec.md's and plan.md's current committed text.
